intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii airport at 11:20 AM — collect luggage, pick up a lei greeting at the terminal, and arrange ground transportation to your accommodation. Take time to freshen up and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby beach for a relaxed first afternoon in Hawaii. Waimea Bay or Ala Moana Beach Park (depending on island) offers free entry, calm waters, and a classic Hawaiian welcome. Bring a towel and soak in the scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beachfront promenade and watch the sunset. Grab a casual dinner at a local plate lunch spot or food truck near the hotel area.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport upon arrival — look for local bakeries or ABC Stores for affordable options (~$5–8)
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In or similar local plate lunch spot — try the loco moco or mixed plate for ~$10–12
meals.dinner: Local food truck or casual diner near hotel — shrimp plate or poke bowl for ~$12–15

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 11:20 AM, nothing is scheduled before arrival. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Pick up a reusable water bottle and sunscreen at an ABC Store to save money throughout the trip. Note: The hotel listed is in Buena Park, CA — confirm your Hawaii accommodation upon booking.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ala Moana Beach Park (free entry) — one of Hawaii's best family-friendly beaches with calm, protected waters, picnic areas, and restrooms. Arrive early to snag a shaded spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a free shuttle to Ala Moana Center for window shopping and affordable food court dining. Then explore the nearby Magic Island lagoon — perfect for kids and families with its calm, enclosed swimming area.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Waikiki Beach for the iconic sunset experience. Watch local hula performances often held for free on the beach. Enjoy the lively atmosphere without spending much.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh fruit and pastries from a local farmers market or ABC Store (~$6–8)
meals.lunch: Ala Moana Food Court — Panda Express, Makai Market, or local Hawaiian options for ~$10–13
meals.dinner: Waikiki Brewing Company happy hour or Marugame Udon for budget-friendly noodles (~$12–15)

day_by_day.notes: August weather averages around 16.8°C (62°F) highs — pack a light layer for evenings. Rain is possible (176mm monthly average), so carry a compact umbrella. All beach activities are free.

day_by_day.morning: Hike Diamond Head State Monument — a world-famous volcanic crater hike with panoramic views of Oahu. Entry is $5/person and the hike takes about 1.5–2 hours round trip. Great for families with older kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cool off at Kaimana Beach (Sans Souci Beach) — a quieter, locals-loved beach near Diamond Head with good snorkeling and calm waters. Bring your own snorkel gear or rent cheaply nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kapiolani Park — free entry, open green space with picnic areas. Catch any free events or just relax under the trees as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Bogart's Cafe near Diamond Head — acai bowls and coffee for ~$10–12
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch from Safeway or Times Supermarket — deli sandwiches, local snacks, and drinks for ~$8–10
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood or Ono Hawaiian Foods — authentic Hawaiian plate lunch style dinner for ~$13–16

day_by_day.notes: Book Diamond Head parking in advance online — parking fills up quickly. Alternatively, take TheBus (public transit) for just $3/ride to save on parking fees. Bring plenty of water for the hike.

day_by_day.morning: Take TheBus to the North Shore — visit Haleiwa Town for a stroll through the charming surf village. Browse local boutiques and art galleries without spending much. Kids will love the laid-back surf culture vibe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Waimea Bay Beach Park for swimming and cliff jumping (for brave adults). The bay is calmer in summer, making it safe for families. Then visit Sunset Beach for a walk and iconic photo ops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Haleiwa for shave ice at Matsumoto's or Aoki's — a must-do Hawaii tradition for ~$4–6. Head back to your accommodation via TheBus.

meals.breakfast: Grab granola bars and fruit from a grocery store the night before for an on-the-go breakfast (~$4–5)
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa — famous garlic shrimp plate for ~$14–16 (iconic North Shore experience)
meals.dinner: Haleiwa Joe's Happy Hour or Kono's Northshore for affordable burritos and plates (~$12–14)

day_by_day.notes: TheBus Route 60 goes to the North Shore from downtown Honolulu — budget $6 round trip per person. The North Shore is about 1 hour away. Waimea Bay cliff jumping is for confident swimmers only — supervise children closely.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — the USS Arizona Memorial is free (boat ride included). Book timed entry passes online in advance as they go fast. An incredibly moving and educational experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free outdoor exhibits at Pearl Harbor — the historic grounds, memorials, and museum displays are all accessible without paying for the paid attractions (USS Missouri, etc.).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Chinatown Honolulu for an affordable and culturally rich evening — browse local markets, art galleries, and enjoy the vibrant neighborhood atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Liliha Bakery — famous for coco puffs and local breakfast plates, ~$10–13
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from the grocery store to eat near Pearl Harbor (~$8–10)
meals.dinner: Chinatown Honolulu — Little Village Noodle House or Fook Yuen for authentic dim sum and noodles, ~$12–15

day_by_day.notes: The USS Arizona Memorial boat ride is free but timed passes must be reserved online at recreation.gov well in advance. Arrive 30 minutes early. The paid attractions (USS Missouri, USS Bowfin) are optional — skip to stay on budget.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Manoa Falls Trail — a lush, jungle rainforest hike leading to a stunning 150-foot waterfall. Trail fee is $5/vehicle. The 1.6-mile round trip is manageable for families with kids 6+.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Lyon Arboretum (free or small donation) adjacent to the trail — beautiful botanical gardens with tropical plants, perfect for a relaxed family walk after the hike.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for the free Kuhio Beach Hula Show — held Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday evenings at the Kuhio Beach Hula Mound. A wonderful free cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at accommodation or grab items from 7-Eleven/ABC Store (~$5–7)
meals.lunch: Manoa Marketplace food options or Andy's Sandwiches & Smoothies near the trail (~$10–12)
meals.dinner: Waikiki — Tikis Grill & Bar happy hour specials or Ramen Nakamura for budget-friendly bowls (~$13–15)

day_by_day.notes: Manoa Falls trail can be muddy — wear closed-toe shoes or water shoes. The forest is lush and beautiful but expect some rain. The hula show schedule should be confirmed locally upon arrival. Check NPS website for any trail closures.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park on the Big Island — take an early inter-island flight (book budget carriers like Southwest or Hawaiian Airlines in advance for ~$60–80 round trip). Explore the Kilauea Caldera and Crater Rim Drive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Kilauea Iki Trail (4-mile loop through a hardened lava lake) or the shorter Devastation Trail (1.2 miles, family-friendly). Visit the Jaggar Museum overlook for spectacular volcanic views. Park entry is $35/vehicle or use an America the Beautiful Pass.
day_by_day.evening: If staying overnight on Big Island, check into a budget hostel or Airbnb. If day-tripping, catch the return flight back to Oahu and enjoy a relaxed dinner near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab airport snacks and coffee before the early flight (~$8–10)
meals.lunch: Volcano House Restaurant (budget option: soup and sandwich) or pack a lunch from a grocery store (~$10–14)
meals.dinner: Café Ono at Volcano or Thai Thai Restaurant in Volcano Village for ~$14–18 (Big Island), OR local plate lunch near Oahu hotel if day-tripping (~$12–14)

day_by_day.notes: This is the Hawaii Volcanoes National Park experience from the available experiences list. Book inter-island flights at least 2–3 weeks ahead for the best budget prices. If budget is tight, consider skipping the inter-island flight and watching volcano documentaries/visiting Bishop Museum instead. Check volcanic activity status at nps.gov/havo before going.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Oahu (if overnighted on Big Island) or enjoy a leisurely morning. Visit Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for world-class snorkeling — book online in advance ($25/adult, children under 12 free). One of Hawaii's best family snorkel spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling or relax on Hanauma Bay's beautiful crescent beach. The protected bay is home to hundreds of tropical fish and sea turtles. Watch the mandatory 9-minute educational video before entering the water.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or bus along the scenic Kalaniana'ole Highway back toward Honolulu. Stop at Halona Blowhole Lookout (free) for dramatic ocean views before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a smoothie and acai bowl from a local cafe near your hotel (~$10–12)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to eat at Hanauma Bay — no outside food vendors inside, so bring your own to save money (~$8–10)
meals.dinner: Koko Marina Center food options or Zippy's Restaurant (local chain, very affordable) for ~$10–13

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations — spots fill up weeks ahead. Entry is $25/adult; children 12 and under are free. The bay is closed on Tuesdays for conservation. Snorkel gear rental is available on-site for ~$12. No sunscreen with oxybenzone allowed — bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Family tickets and discounts available (~$25/adult, $17/child). Explore Hawaiian artifacts, a planetarium, and science exhibits perfect for curious kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kailua Beach on the Windward Coast — consistently rated one of Hawaii's best beaches with turquoise waters and white sand. Rent kayaks to paddle out to the Mokulua Islands (~$30–40/hour for a double kayak) or simply swim and relax for free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kailua Town — charming, local-feeling neighborhood with boutique shops and excellent dining options. Pick up any last souvenirs at affordable local shops.

meals.breakfast: Morning Brew in Kailua or Cinnamon's Restaurant for famous Hawaiian pancakes (~$12–15)
meals.lunch: Kailua Town — Kalapawai Cafe & Deli for fresh sandwiches and salads (~$12–14)
meals.dinner: Lanikai Juice or Poke to the Max in Kailua for healthy, affordable Hawaiian poke bowls (~$13–16)

day_by_day.notes: Kailua Beach has free parking (arrive early) and free beach access. The Bishop Museum is best for families with school-age children. Check for Bishop Museum family discount packages online before visiting. Kailua is about 30 minutes from Waikiki by car or 45 minutes by TheBus.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit your favorite beach or spot for one last swim. Pack up and check out of accommodation. Store luggage at the hotel if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Ala Moana Center or Waikiki — look for affordable macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, and local chocolates at grocery stores (much cheaper than airport shops). Take a final walk along Waikiki Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport for departure. Arrive at least 2–3 hours early for inter-island or mainland flights. Reflect on 10 incredible days in paradise!

meals.breakfast: Local diner or hotel breakfast — eggs, rice, and spam (local staple) for ~$8–10
meals.lunch: Grab a final plate lunch from a local spot or food truck near Waikiki (~$11–13)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or pack snacks for the flight to save money (~$10–15)

day_by_day.notes: Buy any grocery store souvenirs (Kona coffee, macadamia nuts, chocolate) today — prices at the airport are 30–50% higher. Check airline baggage policies if you've purchased items. Return any rental gear. Leave a review for your accommodation to help future budget travelers. Total estimated daily budget: $80–120/person including food, activities, and local transport.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii airport at 11:20 AM via Alaska Airlines — collect luggage, pick up rental car or arrange shuttle transfer to hotel. Check in early if possible or store luggage at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a short drive to a nearby beach for a relaxed first afternoon. Visit Waikiki Beach for a gentle introduction to Hawaii — stroll the shoreline, dip your toes in the warm Pacific, and let the family decompress after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Waikiki strip for dinner. Walk along Kalakaua Avenue and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of the beachfront neighborhood as the sun sets over the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Grab a light snack or coffee at the airport upon arrival — try a local grab-and-go option like a musubi (rice ball with Spam) from an airport kiosk.
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In (Kapahulu Ave) — a beloved local institution serving affordable plate lunches including mixed plates, loco moco, and saimin noodles. Budget-friendly and authentically Hawaiian.
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki — mid-range beachfront restaurant with classic Hawaiian dishes like huli huli chicken and fresh fish. Great ocean views and a relaxed family-friendly atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 11:20 AM, Day 1 is intentionally light. Prioritize rest and gentle exploration. The hotel is located in Buena Park, CA — confirm that Hawaii accommodations are arranged separately as this itinerary assumes the trip is to Hawaii with the Buena Park listing as the departure/return base. Pack reef-safe sunscreen as it is required at many Hawaii beaches and marine reserves.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — arrive early (doors open at 6:45 AM) to beat the crowds and secure entry. This marine sanctuary requires a short educational video before entry. Snorkel among hundreds of tropical fish in crystal-clear, calm waters — perfect for families with children. Reserve timed entry tickets online in advance as daily capacity is strictly limited.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Koko Head Crater area for a scenic coastal drive along the Kalanianaole Highway. Stop at Halona Blowhole Lookout for dramatic ocean spray views, then relax at Sandy Beach Park — a beautiful but wave-active beach ideal for watching local bodyboarders (swimming is for experienced ocean swimmers only).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a relaxed evening. Browse the International Marketplace for souvenirs and local crafts before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a light breakfast at the hotel or grab malasadas (Portuguese-style donuts) from Leonard's Bakery — a Hawaii icon open early and perfect for a sweet morning treat.
meals.lunch: Pikake Terrace at the Hanauma Bay area or pack a picnic lunch to enjoy at the beach. Alternatively, stop at Zippy's Restaurant for affordable local comfort food including chili rice and saimin.
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood (mid-range, cash only) — a small but legendary spot in Kaimuki serving some of Oahu's freshest poke bowls. Arrive early as lines form quickly. Family-friendly and very affordable.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay is closed on Tuesdays, so Monday is the ideal day to visit. Book timed entry tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance at hawaiistateparks.org. Bring water shoes for easier reef navigation. The water temperature is warm year-round at approximately 26–28°C.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — spend a full day at this world-class cultural attraction in Laie on Oahu's North Shore (approximately 1-hour drive from Waikiki). Morning activities include self-guided exploration of the six Polynesian village exhibits representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tonga, and Tahiti. Watch live cultural demonstrations including fire-making, tapa cloth crafting, and traditional cooking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — join interactive canoe tours, participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking and hula lessons, and watch the spectacular afternoon canoe pageant on the lagoon. This is one of the most educational and entertaining family experiences in all of Hawaii.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the Ha: Breath of Life evening show — a breathtaking 90-minute Polynesian theatrical performance featuring fire dancing, traditional music, and stunning choreography. Dinner package options are available on-site.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a local café en route. Try Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua for fluffy pancakes and eggs if time allows on the drive north.
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included in most package tickets. Features a wide spread of Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes including kalua pork, poi, fresh fruit, and island desserts.
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau Dinner Package at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a traditional luau-style dinner with imu-roasted pig, lomi salmon, haupia coconut pudding, and more. Bundled with the evening show for great value.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase combination packages online in advance for significant savings. The All-Inclusive Ambassador Package is the best value for families. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the grounds are expansive. The center is closed on Sundays. Allow the full day — rushing this experience would be a disservice to its richness.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — dive deep into authentic Hawaiian food culture with a self-guided or guided plate lunch tour across Honolulu's most iconic local eateries. Start at Helena's Hawaiian Food in Kalihi (open Tuesday–Friday) for traditional dishes like pipikaula (dried beef), laulau, and poi that have been served since 1946.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Iolani Palace — the only official royal palace in the United States, offering guided tours of the beautifully restored residence of Hawaii's last monarchs. Afterward, stroll through downtown Honolulu's historic Chinatown district, browsing local markets, art galleries, and lei stands.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ala Moana Beach Park for a golden-hour sunset stroll along the calm, family-friendly shoreline. The adjacent Ala Moana Center (largest open-air shopping mall in the world) offers great options for a casual dinner and light shopping.

meals.breakfast: Café Kaila in Market City Shopping Center — known as one of Oahu's best breakfast spots, serving creative egg dishes, fluffy pancakes, and fresh-pressed juices. Arrive early as waits can be long.
meals.lunch: Helena's Hawaiian Food — the centerpiece of the food tour. Order the combination plate for the most comprehensive tasting experience. Cash only, arrive early as they sell out of certain dishes.
meals.dinner: Mariposa at Neiman Marcus in Ala Moana Center — slightly upscale but accessible mid-range option with beautiful views, fresh island cuisine, and a legendary popovers service. Alternatively, try Goma Tei for excellent ramen in a family-friendly setting.

day_by_day.notes: Helena's Hawaiian Food is closed on weekends and Mondays — Wednesday works perfectly. The plate lunch food tour is a wonderful way to connect with authentic local culture beyond tourist-facing restaurants. Iolani Palace tours should be reserved online in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Take an inter-island flight to Maui (approximately 30–40 minutes). Several daily flights operate between Honolulu and Kahului Airport. Upon arrival, pick up a rental car and drive to the resort town of Lahaina. Explore the historic Lahaina Front Street, browse local art galleries, and visit the famous 150-year-old Banyan Tree — the largest in the United States.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — drive just 5 minutes north of Lahaina to Kaanapali Beach, consistently ranked among America's most beautiful beaches. Spend the afternoon swimming in the calm, warm turquoise waters, building sandcastles, and relaxing under beach umbrellas. Rent snorkel gear from a beachside vendor to explore the reef near Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Cliff Dive at Black Rock — a nightly ceremony at the Sheraton Maui where a torch lighter dives from the cliff into the ocean at sunset, a tradition rooted in Hawaiian legend. Stroll Kaanapali's Beachwalk for a leisurely dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the Honolulu airport before your morning flight — try a local plate from one of the terminal's local food vendors.
meals.lunch: Aloha Mixed Plate in Lahaina — a beloved outdoor beachfront restaurant serving affordable Hawaiian plate lunches with spectacular ocean views. The coconut shrimp and kalua pork plates are outstanding.
meals.dinner: Hula Grill Kaanapali — a mid-range beachfront restaurant directly on Kaanapali Beach serving fresh Hawaiian fish, wood-grilled meats, and tropical cocktails. Barefoot Bar area is casual and family-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights with Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest Hawaii for the best rates — book well in advance. If visiting Lahaina, be respectful as the town was significantly impacted by the devastating 2023 wildfires; the community is rebuilding. Check current conditions and access restrictions before visiting specific areas of Lahaina.

day_by_day.morning: Road to Hana — begin the iconic scenic drive along Maui's northeastern coastline. Start early from Kaanapali (approximately 1.5 hours to the start of the route in Paia). Stop at Twin Falls for an easy family-friendly waterfall hike, then continue to the Garden of Eden Arboretum for lush tropical gardens and ocean overlooks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana stopping at Wailua Falls, the black sand beach at Wai'anapanapa State Park (advance reservations required), and the beautiful Hamoa Beach near Hana town. The drive features 59 bridges and dramatic coastal scenery at every turn.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive from Hana or stay overnight in Hana for a more relaxed pace (optional). If returning, the drive back takes approximately 2.5–3 hours. Enjoy a quiet dinner in Paia town.

meals.breakfast: Cafe des Amis in Paia — a charming café serving crepes, smoothie bowls, and coffee. Perfect starting point before the Hana drive.
meals.lunch: Roadside food stands along the Road to Hana — look for fresh banana bread at Aunty Sandy's in Keanae (a legendary stop), fresh coconut, and fruit smoothies from family-run roadside stands. This is part of the authentic experience.
meals.dinner: Flatbread Company in Paia — wood-fired organic pizzas with local Hawaiian toppings in a lively, family-friendly atmosphere. Great value and consistently excellent.

day_by_day.notes: Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance reservations at hawaiistateparks.org — book several weeks ahead. Start the drive before 8:00 AM to avoid traffic and maximize daylight. Fill your gas tank in Paia as there are no gas stations along the Hana Highway. Pack snacks, water, and motion sickness medication for children if needed as the road is very winding.

day_by_day.morning: Take an inter-island flight from Maui to the Big Island of Hawaii (Kona or Hilo Airport — Hilo is closer to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park). Fly into Hilo for the most convenient access. Upon arrival, drive directly to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (approximately 45 minutes from Hilo).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration — witness the awe-inspiring power of Kilauea, one of the world's most active volcanoes. Drive the Crater Rim Drive for panoramic caldera views, walk the Devastation Trail through a surreal landscape of hardened lava, and explore the Thurston Lava Tube — a naturally formed tunnel through ancient lava flows that children find absolutely magical.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hilo for the evening. If lava is actively flowing (check NPS.gov for current conditions), join a ranger-led evening lava viewing program for an unforgettable sight of glowing lava against the night sky.

meals.breakfast: Airport breakfast or a quick stop at a Hilo café upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Cafe Ono at the Volcano Art Center inside the national park — light sandwiches, soups, and snacks in a beautiful setting surrounded by native ohia forest.
meals.dinner: Hilo Bay Cafe — a beloved Hilo institution serving locally sourced Hawaiian fusion cuisine including fresh poke, grass-fed beef, and seasonal vegetable dishes. Mid-range pricing with excellent quality.

day_by_day.notes: Always check current volcanic activity and trail conditions at nps.gov/havo before visiting. Some areas may be closed due to volcanic emissions (sulfur dioxide). Bring light jackets as the elevation at the park (approximately 1,200 meters) makes it noticeably cooler than the coast — temperatures can drop to 15°C or lower, especially in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Hilo side of the Big Island — visit Rainbow Falls (Waianuenue), a stunning 24-meter waterfall just minutes from downtown Hilo where rainbows frequently appear in the morning mist. Afterward, browse the Hilo Farmers Market (open daily but largest on Wednesdays and Saturdays — Sunday still has good vendors) for fresh tropical fruits, local honey, macadamia nut products, and handmade crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive up to Mauna Kea Visitor Information Station at 2,800 meters elevation (do not drive to the summit without a 4WD vehicle). The visitor center offers stunning views above the cloud line and fascinating astronomy exhibits. This is a wonderful family educational experience. Note: the drive takes approximately 1.5 hours from Hilo. Acclimatize at the visitor station before considering the summit.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hilo for a relaxed evening. Take a sunset walk along Hilo Bay's waterfront park.

meals.breakfast: Ken's House of Pancakes in Hilo — a 24-hour local diner serving massive portions of pancakes, eggs, and loco moco. A Big Island institution beloved by locals and visitors alike.
meals.lunch: Poke to the Max in Hilo — build-your-own poke bowls with fresh local fish, various marinades, and toppings. Excellent value and authentically Hawaiian.
meals.dinner: Cafe Pesto in downtown Hilo — wood-fired pizzas and fresh island seafood in a historic building. Family-friendly with a diverse menu that satisfies all palates.

day_by_day.notes: Children under 13 and pregnant women should not go above the Mauna Kea Visitor Information Station due to altitude. Bring warm layers for the visitor station — temperatures at 2,800 meters are significantly colder. The visitor station hosts free stargazing programs on clear evenings starting at 6:00 PM — one of the best free activities in all of Hawaii.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Kona side of the Big Island (approximately 2–2.5 hours). Stop at Punalu'u Black Sand Beach on the way — a dramatic black volcanic sand beach where Hawaiian green sea turtles (honu) regularly bask on the shore. This is one of the most unique beach experiences in Hawaii and a favorite with families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kailua-Kona and spend the afternoon at Kahalu'u Beach Park — one of the Big Island's best snorkeling beaches, calm and shallow enough for children. Sea turtles are frequently spotted here as well. Rent snorkel gear from the adjacent beach shack. Afterward, explore Kailua-Kona's historic waterfront, including Hulihe'e Palace and Mokuaikaua Church.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Kailua-Kona's vibrant waterfront Ali'i Drive for the final evening on the Big Island. Browse local shops, watch the sunset over the Pacific, and enjoy a celebratory family dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Hilo hotel before departure — or stop at Punalu'u Bake Shop near the black sand beach for famous sweetbread and malasadas.
meals.lunch: Island Lava Java in Kailua-Kona — a casual beachfront café with excellent sandwiches, salads, and fresh coffee. Outdoor seating with stunning ocean views.
meals.dinner: Huggo's on the Rocks in Kailua-Kona — a beloved open-air oceanfront restaurant perched directly over the water. Fresh catch of the day, lobster, and Hawaiian specialties in a magical setting. Mid-range to slightly upscale but perfect for a special family dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Do not touch or disturb the sea turtles at Punalu'u or Kahalu'u — it is illegal under the Endangered Species Act and carries significant fines. Maintain a distance of at least 3 meters. The turtles are remarkably calm and will often swim directly past snorkelers at Kahalu'u Beach.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Big Island — take an early morning coffee farm tour in the Kona Coffee Belt (the only coffee-growing region in the United States). Tours at farms like Mountain Thunder Coffee Plantation or Greenwell Farms are free or low-cost and offer fascinating insight into the world-renowned Kona coffee production process. Purchase fresh-roasted beans as a perfect souvenir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kona International Airport for your return inter-island flight to Honolulu, then connect to your mainland flight home. Allow plenty of time for check-in and security. Use any layover time in Honolulu to pick up last-minute souvenirs at the airport's local vendor shops — look for local chocolates, macadamia nuts, and aloha wear.
day_by_day.evening: Return flight home — reflect on an incredible 10-day Hawaii adventure filled with volcanic landscapes, pristine beaches, rich Polynesian culture, and unforgettable family memories.

meals.breakfast: Lemongrass Restaurant in Kailua-Kona for a final island breakfast — fresh tropical fruit plates, eggs, and Kona coffee. The perfect send-off meal.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Kona airport or Honolulu airport during layover — grab a final poke bowl or plate lunch from one of the terminal's local food options.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or dinner at home upon return.

day_by_day.notes: Check airline baggage policies for bringing home food items — fresh fruits and plants from Hawaii are restricted from leaving the state due to agricultural regulations. Commercially packaged items like coffee, macadamia nuts, and chocolate are perfectly fine to bring home. Arrive at Kona Airport at least 2 hours before departure. This concludes a beautifully balanced 10-day Hawaii itinerary spanning Oahu, Maui, and the Big Island.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Honolulu International Airport at 11:20 AM via Alaska Airlines. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your premium hotel in Waikiki. Check-in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll along Waikiki Beach. Rent premium beach chairs and umbrellas through the hotel concierge. Enjoy the warm Pacific waters and iconic Diamond Head views as a gentle introduction to Hawaii.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the ocean, followed by a welcome dinner celebrating the start of your Hawaiian adventure.

meals.breakfast: Light snack on the plane or at the airport — grab a coffee and pastry at an airport lounge before landing.
meals.lunch: Azure Restaurant at the Royal Hawaiian Hotel — oceanfront dining with fresh island seafood and stunning Waikiki views.
meals.dinner: Nobu Honolulu — world-class Japanese-Peruvian fusion by celebrity chef Nobu Matsuhisa; ideal for a luxurious first-night celebration.

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 11:20 AM, no morning activities are scheduled. Allow 1–1.5 hours for baggage and transfer. Pre-arrange private airport transfer through the hotel concierge for a seamless arrival experience. Pack light beach essentials in your carry-on for easy afternoon access.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — arrive early (8:00 AM recommended) to beat crowds at one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries. Watch the mandatory conservation video, then snorkel among hundreds of tropical fish species in crystal-clear waters. Rent premium snorkel gear on-site or bring your own.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Makapuu Coastal Trail for panoramic ocean views, then visit Sea Life Park Hawaii for family-friendly marine encounters including dolphin interactions and penguin exhibits — a perfect activity for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a beachside luau experience or sunset catamaran cruise along the Waikiki coastline.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast or hotel buffet — start early to make the most of Hanauma Bay's morning hours.
meals.lunch: Kona Brewing Company Waikiki — casual yet premium craft beers and fresh island-inspired burgers and flatbreads with ocean views.
meals.dinner: House Without a Key at the Halekulani Hotel — iconic open-air dining under a century-old kiawe tree with live Hawaiian music and hula performance at sunset.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations — book at least 2–3 days ahead. Entry fee applies per person. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only. Bring water shoes for the reef entry. August weather may bring occasional afternoon showers (176mm monthly average), so carry a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — depart early for the 35-mile drive to Laie on the North Shore of Oahu. Spend the morning exploring six authentic Polynesian village exhibits representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Participate in hands-on cultural demonstrations including fire-making, coconut husking, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at the Polynesian Cultural Center — enjoy the thrilling 'Ha: Breath of Life' rehearsal preview, canoe pageant on the lagoon, and interactive family activities. The Ambassador VIP package includes guided tours and reserved seating.
day_by_day.evening: The spectacular 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show — a world-class Polynesian theatrical production with fire dancing, acrobatics, and live music. One of Hawaii's premier entertainment experiences.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — or grab fresh malasadas (Portuguese doughnuts) from Leonard's Bakery en route.
meals.lunch: Ali'i Luau buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — an all-inclusive feast of traditional Polynesian and Hawaiian dishes including kalua pork, poi, and haupia.
meals.dinner: Gateway Restaurant at the Polynesian Cultural Center — premium dinner package included with the Ambassador VIP evening show experience.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ambassador VIP package for the best experience — it includes priority access, guided tours, and premium show seating. The full-day experience runs approximately 12:00 PM to 9:30 PM. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The drive from Waikiki takes about 45–55 minutes. This is one of Hawaii's top family experiences and well worth the full day.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — embark on a guided culinary journey through Honolulu's most iconic local eateries. Visit legendary spots serving plate lunches featuring two-scoop rice, macaroni salad, and proteins like shoyu chicken, loco moco, and kalbi short ribs. Explore neighborhoods like Chinatown and Kalihi for authentic flavors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Explore the Hawaiian Hall with priceless royal artifacts, volcanic geology exhibits, and a spectacular planetarium show. Excellent for families with educational and interactive displays.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ala Moana Center — the world's largest open-air shopping mall — for premium shopping at luxury boutiques including Chanel, Louis Vuitton, and Tiffany & Co. Enjoy the nightly sunset over Ala Moana Beach Park.

meals.breakfast: Eggs 'n Things Waikiki — a beloved Honolulu institution famous for enormous fluffy pancakes with whipped cream and macadamia nut syrup.
meals.lunch: Plate lunch food tour covers multiple tastings — Helena's Hawaiian Food (James Beard Award winner) for pipikaula short ribs and lomi salmon.
meals.dinner: MW Restaurant by Chef Michelle Myung-Ja Karr-Ueoka — contemporary Hawaii Regional Cuisine using locally sourced ingredients; one of Honolulu's most acclaimed fine dining destinations.

day_by_day.notes: The plate lunch food tour is best experienced on a weekday when local spots are fully operational. Book a guided food tour through a reputable local operator for insider access. Bishop Museum is closed on Tuesdays. Ala Moana Center is open until 9 PM most evenings. Keep an umbrella handy for afternoon showers.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Honolulu (HNL) to Maui (OGG) — short inter-island flight approximately 30–40 minutes. Book a premium cabin or charter flight. Transfer via private car to Kaanapali Beach resort area on Maui's west coast. Check into a luxury beachfront resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — settle onto one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand. Rent premium beach equipment, try stand-up paddleboarding, outrigger canoe rides, or simply relax in the warm turquoise waters. Explore Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) for excellent snorkeling.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Cliff Diving Ceremony at Black Rock — a nightly tradition at the Sheraton Maui where a torch-lit diver leaps from the lava rock formation at sunset, honoring ancient Hawaiian warriors.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before flying — or Heavenly Island Lifestyle restaurant in Waikiki for a healthy açaí bowl and avocado toast.
meals.lunch: Leilani's on the Beach at Whalers Village, Kaanapali — casual fine dining with fresh fish tacos, lobster bisque, and stunning beachfront views.
meals.dinner: Japengo at the Hyatt Regency Maui — award-winning Pacific Rim cuisine with fresh sushi, sashimi, and innovative Japanese-Hawaiian fusion dishes overlooking the ocean.

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights at least 2 weeks in advance. Hawaiian Airlines and Mokulele Airlines offer frequent inter-island service. Kaanapali Beach can get busy in August — arrive early to secure premium beach spots. The cliff diving ceremony begins around sunset (approximately 7:00–7:30 PM in August). Pre-book resort beach equipment through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Road to Hana Drive — depart at 6:00 AM for this legendary scenic highway. Stop at Twin Falls for a refreshing waterfall swim, explore the Garden of Eden Arboretum, and marvel at the stunning black sand beaches at Waianapanapa State Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Hana Town — explore the charming village, visit the Hana Cultural Center, and stop at Wailua Falls. Enjoy the lush rainforest scenery and dramatic coastal cliffs. Optional: continue to the stunning Pools of Oheo (Seven Sacred Pools) in Haleakala National Park.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive along the southern route (Piilani Highway) for different scenic views, or stay overnight in Hana at a luxury boutique property for a more relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed gourmet breakfast box from the resort — enjoy at Twin Falls or a scenic roadside stop.
meals.lunch: Coconut Glen's Organic Ice Cream (roadside stop) for exotic tropical flavors, plus Nahiku Marketplace for fresh fish tacos and local snacks.
meals.dinner: Hana Ranch Restaurant in Hana Town — farm-to-table dining using locally raised beef and garden-fresh produce in a beautiful ranch setting.

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is approximately 65 miles with 620 curves and 59 bridges — allow 3–4 hours each way. Start very early to avoid traffic. Rent a premium SUV or jeep for comfort. Download the 'Road to Hana' app for GPS-guided audio commentary. Waianapanapa State Park requires advance reservations. Carry cash for roadside stands. Pack rain gear as this is one of Maui's wettest areas.

day_by_day.morning: Haleakala Crater Sunrise Experience — wake at 2:30 AM for the drive to the summit of Haleakala volcano (10,023 feet). Watch the breathtaking sunrise above the clouds — one of Hawaii's most awe-inspiring natural spectacles. Explore the lunar-like crater landscape and learn about the unique silversword plants found nowhere else on Earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Upcountry Maui — visit Surfing Goat Dairy for a fun family farm tour and artisan cheese tasting, then explore the charming town of Makawao with its boutique galleries and paniolo (Hawaiian cowboy) heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kaanapali for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a private beachside bonfire experience arranged through the resort concierge, with s'mores and Hawaiian storytelling.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise snacks and hot coffee/cocoa at the Haleakala summit visitor center — pack warm layers as temperatures near the summit can drop to 5–10°C.
meals.lunch: Cafe des Amis in Paia Town — eclectic Mediterranean-Indian fusion with fresh crepes, curries, and organic salads; a beloved Maui institution.
meals.dinner: Merriman's Maui at Kapalua — farm-to-table pioneer Peter Merriman's signature restaurant with panoramic ocean views and Hawaii Regional Cuisine at its finest.

day_by_day.notes: Haleakala sunrise reservations are MANDATORY and must be booked through recreation.gov up to 60 days in advance — this sells out extremely fast. Summit temperatures can be near freezing; bring warm layers, gloves, and a windbreaker. The drive to the summit takes approximately 1.5 hours from Kaanapali. Check weather forecasts — occasional cloud cover can obscure the sunrise.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Maui (OGG) to Kona (KOA) on the Big Island — approximately 45-minute inter-island flight. Transfer to your luxury resort along the Kohala Coast. Enjoy the resort's premium amenities — most Kohala Coast resorts feature world-class pools, spas, and private beach access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration — drive approximately 1.5 hours to the park. Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes. Walk the Kilauea Iki Trail through a solidified lava lake, visit the Thurston Lava Tube, and view the dramatic Halema'uma'u Crater at the Thomas A. Jaggar Museum overlook.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the magical glow of the Halema'uma'u Crater after dark — the lava lake illuminates the night sky with an otherworldly orange glow, weather permitting. This is one of Hawaii's most unforgettable natural spectacles.

meals.breakfast: In-flight snack or early hotel breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Volcano House Restaurant inside Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — the only restaurant within the park, offering stunning crater views and fresh island-inspired cuisine.
meals.dinner: Brown's Beach House at the Fairmont Orchid — one of the Big Island's most romantic and acclaimed restaurants with oceanfront dining and exceptional Hawaiian Regional Cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Check the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory website for current volcanic activity before visiting. The park entrance fee is $30 per vehicle (valid 7 days). Wear closed-toe shoes for lava field walking. Volcanic smog (vog) can affect air quality — those with respiratory conditions should check vog forecasts. The evening crater glow is best viewed from the Jaggar Museum overlook. Bring a flashlight and warm layer for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Manta Ray Night Snorkel Experience — book a premium guided tour departing from Keauhou Bay. Snorkel above aggregations of giant Pacific manta rays (wingspans up to 14 feet) that gather nightly to feed on plankton attracted by dive lights. One of Hawaii's most extraordinary wildlife encounters, suitable for families with children 8+.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kona Town — visit the historic Hulihe'e Palace (former Hawaiian royal summer retreat), browse the charming Ali'i Drive waterfront, and stop at the Original Kona Coffee Living History Farm to learn about Kona's world-famous coffee heritage with a premium tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise along the Kohala Coast aboard a luxury catamaran — sip champagne, enjoy gourmet appetizers, and watch for spinner dolphins and humpback whale activity (seasonal) as the sun dips below the Pacific horizon.

meals.breakfast: Daylight Mind Coffee Company in Kailua-Kona — farm-to-cup Kona coffee with avocado toast and fresh-baked pastries in a stunning oceanfront setting.
meals.lunch: Jackie Rey's Ohana Grill in Kona — beloved local institution with fresh catch specials, macadamia nut-crusted fish, and generous portions in a warm family atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Canoe House at the Mauna Lani Resort — legendary Big Island fine dining institution with an open-air oceanfront setting, James Beard-recognized cuisine, and an exceptional wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Manta ray tours must be booked well in advance — operators like Manta Ray Advocates and Jack's Diving Locker offer premium guided experiences. The tour typically departs around 5:30–6:00 PM. Manta ray sightings are not guaranteed but have a very high success rate (85%+). Children must be comfortable snorkeling in open water at night. Bring a waterproof camera or GoPro for incredible footage.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Big Island — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and last swim at the resort beach or pool. Visit Hapuna Beach State Recreation Area — consistently ranked among America's top beaches with brilliant white sand and calm, clear waters perfect for a final family swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium souvenir shopping and last-minute experiences — visit the Shops at Mauna Lani for luxury Hawaiian goods, Kona coffee, macadamia nut products, and authentic aloha wear. Optional: book a final spa treatment at your resort's world-class spa for ultimate relaxation before travel.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Kona International Airport (KOA) for departure flight. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day Hawaiian journey filled with cultural immersion, natural wonders, and unforgettable family memories.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — indulge in a full Hawaiian breakfast spread with fresh tropical fruits, loco moco, and Kona coffee.
meals.lunch: Pueo's Osteria in Waimea (en route to airport) — James Beard-nominated Italian-Hawaiian fusion with handmade pasta and locally sourced ingredients; a hidden Big Island gem.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Kona International Airport or an early dinner before departure — Island Lava Java in Kailua-Kona for a casual but delicious farewell meal with ocean views.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure at Kona Airport as inter-island connections may require additional processing. Arrange private car transfer from resort to airport through the concierge. Declare all agricultural items (fresh fruits, plants, leis) before leaving Hawaii — strict USDA regulations apply. Consider shipping home premium purchases like Kona coffee and macadamia nuts to avoid baggage weight issues. Mahalo for an incredible Hawaiian adventure!
